main_text.p: ribus & vinum felle, qui Me torquent potius quàm docent, & quorum ora in acerba convitia, quàm in amicas preces, promptiora.

p.i: Tu (Domine Veritatis) nosti, quàm frequen-ter Sacras tuas Scripturas in perniciem meam pervertunt. Cum nil hîc difcrtius præcipiatur, quàm ut pareant mihi simul, & incolumem con-servent. O ne sit Illis in condemnationem.
Nosti Domine nonnullos qui Orationes longas orantes fratrum suorum Domos, & Regus, & Dei denique comederunt.
Oleum eorum ne offendat Caput meum, nec Corroborantia Pharmaca Cor meum opprimant, contra iniquitatem eorum semper precabor.

A Veneno sub linguis eorum, à labiorum Il-lorum laqueis, ab Igne Verborum & Gladiis libera Me semper (Domine) & mecum unà illos fido & pio Corde, qui bene volunt animæ meæ, & prosperitate illius delectantur, quíque suis orationibus sublevare quærunt hanc mæstitiam Famuli Tui & solitudinem, Deus meus, & Rex meus.

page.notes: The "25." before the catchword is uncertain and not included in the catchword. The word "Regus" is printed that way and is kept as printed. Stains and the black rule are not text and are left out. The large initial "A" of "A Veneno" is set as printed. Greek running head is transcribed in Greek letters as printed.
